newsitem.title: GERMANY: GERMAN PROSECUTORS PROBE EMBEZZLEMENT IN GRAF CASE.
newsitem.headline: GERMAN PROSECUTORS PROBE EMBEZZLEMENT IN GRAF CASE.

text.p: German prosecutors are investigating whether the former tax adviser to world number one tennis player Steffi Graf embezzled millions of marks (dollars) from her earnings, the news magazine Focus said on Sunday.
Joachim Eckardt is a former family tax adviser who last month was convicted alongside Steffi's father Peter Graf and received a two and one half year jail sentence for complicity in tax evasion.
Eckardt's lawyer Bernd Schneider, commenting on the prosecutor's allegation, said his client did not take a single penny from Steffi Graf.
"My client did not take or embezzle a single penny from the Graf side," Schneider told Focus.
"There is a separate investigation of Joachim Eckardt in which we have to find out whether he embezzled funds or committed another illegal act," state prosecutor Hubert Jobski told the magazine.
He said that prosecutors had come across the "irregularities" during their tax evasion investigation.

The magazine quotes a Graf family adviser who said that the money had disappeared and said Eckardt was unable to say where the funds had gone. The newsweekly said the family was trying to reach an out-of-court agreement with Eckardt, but was threatening a civil suit if the money was not returned.
A German court in Mannheim sentenced Graf's father on six counts of actual and attempted tax evasion last month.
Peter Graf was sentenced to three years and nine months in jail for evading 12 million marks ($7.3 million) of tax on his daughter's earnings.

Steffi Graf, whose career earnings are estimated at more than $61 million, has told tax investigators she entrusted her financial affairs to her father from an early age and had little idea how her money was managed. ($1=1.6326 Mark)
